/-!
# Erdős Problem 559

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/559](https://www.erdosproblems.com/559)
- [Be83b] Beck, József, _On size Ramsey number of paths, trees, and circuits. I_. J. Graph
  Theory (1983), 115-129.
- [FrPi87] Friedman, J. and Pippenger, N., _Expanding graphs contain all small trees_.
  Combinatorica (1987), 71-76.
- [HKL95] Haxell, P. E. and Kohayakawa, Y. and Łuczak, T., _The induced size-Ramsey number of
  cycles_. Combin. Probab. Comput. (1995), 217-239.
- [RoSz00] Rödl, Vojtěch and Szemerédi, Endre, _On size Ramsey numbers of graphs with bounded
  degree_. Combinatorica (2000), 257-262.
- [Ti22b] Tikhomirov, K., _On bounded degree graphs with large size-Ramsey numbers_.
  arXiv:2210.05818 (2022).
- [DrPe22] N. Draganić and K. Petrova, _Size-Ramsey numbers of graphs with maximum degree three_.
  arXiv:2207.05048 (2022).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos559

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

If $G$ has $n$ vertices and maximum degree $d$ then prove that
$$\hat{R}(G)\ll_d n.$$

This was disproved for $d=3$ by Rödl and Szemerédi [RoSz00], who constructed a graph on $n$
vertices with maximum degree $3$ such that $\hat{R}(G)\gg n(\log n)^{c}$ for some absolute
constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos559.lean#L1275"]
theorem erdos_559 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ d : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.maxDegree ≤ d → (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- Rödl and Szemerédi [RoSz00] disproved the linear bound already for maximum degree $3$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos559.lean#L1275"]
theorem erdos_559.variants.degree_three :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.maxDegree ≤ 3 → (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- Rödl and Szemerédi [RoSz00] constructed, for infinitely many $n$, a graph on $n$ vertices
with maximum degree $3$ such that $\hat{R}(G)\gg n(\log n)^{c}$ for some absolute constant
$c>0$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_559.variants.rodl_szemeredi :
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.maxDegree ≤ 3 ∧ C * n * (log n) ^ c ≤ sizeRamsey G G := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- Tikhomirov [Ti22b] improved this to $\hat{R}(G)\gg n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_559.variants.tikhomirov :
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.maxDegree ≤ 3 ∧ C * n * exp (c * √(log n)) ≤ sizeRamsey G G := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- Friedman and Pippenger [FrPi87] proved the linear bound when $G$ is a tree. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_559.variants.trees (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.IsTree → G.maxDegree ≤ d → (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- The best known upper bound for graphs of maximum degree $3$ is $\hat{R}(G)\leq n^{3/2+o(1)}$,
due to Draganić and Petrova [DrPe22]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_559.variants.draganic_petrova (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.maxDegree ≤ 3 → (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 + ε : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos559

findings.description: The unannotated exponent `c` in `∃ c > 0` is inferred as `ℕ`, not `ℝ`. Lean therefore requires a positive integer logarithmic exponent. For sufficiently large n, every such exponent gives at least an n·log(n) lower bound; I proved in the scratch file that the displayed existential statement is equivalent to its exponent-1 version. The cited Rödl–Szemerédi bound permits a small positive real exponent, specifically 1/60. The stronger integer-exponent claim follows from later work, but does not faithfully state the cited bound.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/559 states the lower bound n(log n)^c for some absolute c>0. Tikhomirov, arXiv:2210.05818v2, abstract and §1, explicitly identifies the Rödl–Szemerédi bound as c·n·(log n)^(1/60). Draganić–Petrova, arXiv:2207.05048v2, §1, gives the same exponent.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the exponent as real: `∃ (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ...`. Then `(log n) ^ c` uses real exponentiation and allows the cited exponent 1/60.

findings.description: Independently of the exponent-type error, `∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop` records examples only for an unbounded subsequence of vertex counts. The cited quantitative result supplies examples for every sufficiently large vertex count. This loses the uniform-in-n lower bound. The docstring explicitly chooses 'infinitely many n', so this may be an intentional weaker corollary rather than an accidental mistranslation, but that choice merits clarification.
findings.source_evidence: Tikhomirov, arXiv:2210.05818v2, abstract and §1, says Rödl and Szemerédi constructed 'for every n≥1' an n-vertex graph of maximum degree at most three with size-Ramsey number at least c·n·(log n)^(1/60). Draganić–Petrova, arXiv:2207.05048v2, §1, likewise says 'for every n'.
findings.suggested_fix: To record the full asymptotic lower bound, replace `∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop` with `∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop` and update the docstring to 'for all sufficiently large n'. Otherwise explicitly identify the declaration as only the infinitely-many-n corollary of the cited theorem.

findings.description: The `∃ᶠ n` quantifier retains only infinitely many sizes, whereas Tikhomirov's theorem gives the quantitative lower bound for every sufficiently large size. An unbounded subsequence does not itself provide that uniform lower bound. This can be a defensible choice of a weaker corollary, especially given the preceding variant's docstring, but it is not an equivalent formulation of the full cited theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Tikhomirov, arXiv:2210.05818v2, Theorem 1.1: 'For every n≥1 there is a graph G′ on n vertices of maximum degree at most three such that r̂(G′)≥cn exp(c√(log n)), for a universal constant c>0.' Its proof begins with an arbitrary sufficiently large integer n.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop` in place of `∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop` to state the full asymptotic result without finite-size boundary issues. Alternatively clarify that only an infinitely-many-n corollary is being recorded.

reformulations.difference: The source writes the uniform upper bound as n^(3/2+o(1)); Lean instead quantifies over every real ε>0 and requires the bound n^(3/2+ε) eventually, uniformly over all subcubic graphs of that order.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is the standard epsilon formulation of the stated upper bound. A vanishing exponent error is eventually at most any fixed ε>0. Conversely, apply the Lean bounds to the maximum size-Ramsey number over the finite set of subcubic graphs on n vertices: for n≥2, the nonnegative part of log(max(1,M(n)))/log(n)−3/2 tends to zero and supplies a vanishing exponent error. Any fixed multiplicative constants are absorbed by an arbitrarily small increase in the exponent.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/559 — mathematical text and current status, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/559 with the HTML response preserving formulas
https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05818 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2210.05818 — Tikhomirov, version 2; abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and its proof
https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05048 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2207.05048 — Draganić–Petrova, version 2; abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and bibliography
https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jgt.3190070115 — Beck's publisher-supplied abstract and bibliographic metadata

Haxell, Kohayakawa and Łuczak, The induced size-Ramsey number of cycles, Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 4 (1995), 217–239, DOI 10.1017/S0963548300001619 — publisher-supplied abstract retrieved through Crossref
review.notes: Checked all six declarations. The main negative answer and the degree-three statement match the source's disproved status. I compiled the exact linked proof and its Ramsey dependency, then proved a bridge from its Nat.find-based invariant and natural coefficients to this repository's sInf-based invariant and real coefficients. The resulting exact main and degree-three statements depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Boundary checks established sizeRamsey(⊥,⊥)=0 for every finite vertex type and sizeRamsey(K₂,K₂)=1, and tested maximum degrees on the smallest graphs. No default-value defect was found. The two quantifier findings are marked questionable because they may deliberately record weaker corollaries. Full text of the older journal papers was not accessible; their relevant claims were cross-checked against the UCSD collection and explicit restatements in the downloaded arXiv sources.

not_demonstrated.reason: The inferred natural exponent is confirmed, but the resulting statement requires a genuine Ω(n log n) size-Ramsey lower bound. It is true by Tikhomirov’s stronger result, not false or vacuous, and proving it requires substantial mathematics. Type inspection or an equivalence with the exponent-1 formulation would not constitute the requested proof or disproof.

submission.summary: Rechecked the elaborated type without invoking any admitted theorem as a proof. No trivial_proof.lean was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: The reported exponent-domain mismatch does not yield a short, honest proof or counterexample to the declaration as stated. Using the imported admitted theorem, or its admitted stronger variant, would not provide an independent proof.

submission.summary: Explicitly typed the positive exponent c as ℝ, so the logarithmic power uses real exponentiation and permits fractional exponents such as 1/60. All other statements and metadata remain unchanged. The edited file compiles with only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
